title: Franks Minstrels and the Alabama Minstrels under Jeff Smith
summary: White began touring with minstrel shows, joining Jeff Smith's Alabama Minstrels and praising Smith as a cornet soloist.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, so I took a portion of the band down there, 11 fellas, and we played this Uncle Tom's Cabin production there. Well, then I began to trek around the country with circuses and minstrel shows and so forth. My first minstrel show was the Franks New York Minstrels out of Birmingham, Alabama. In 1914, I went off on a tour with that minstrel show. But the show busted up after coming out through Virginia into Tennessee. They busted up in a little town called Pulaski, Tennessee. And then I taught a little band in Pulaski during the winter there in Dixon, Pulaski, and Columbia, each. These three little towns. They weren't no more than about nine miles apart from different directors around. But when the warm months, months began to get warm, I looked for another show. And you could always find lucrative work in the Billboard, which was a show publication. Oh, yeah. So I joined up with the Alabama Minstrels. And for a season on the Alabama Minstrels, I was with Jeff Smith under his direction. One of the greatest musicians I have ever known in my life. Fine cornet soloists, the best I've ever listened to. And a wonderful interpreter of the concert scores. Something that I didn't actually get a whole lot of, that is the larger compositions, in the orphanage. The point is they didn't play heavy overtures, but we played modern
songs and marches. How big a band did those minstrel shows have?
Well, Jeff at that time had 24 pieces. 24 pieces.
